name: Hormones in reproduction, contraception and infertility

terms.definition: The main female reproductive hormone, made in the ovaries; it makes the uterus lining build up after menstruation.
terms.examiner: Higher tier: oestrogen inhibits FSH and stimulates LH.

terms.definition: The main male reproductive hormone, made by the testes; it stimulates sperm production.
Follicle stimulating hormone from the pituitary gland; it causes an egg to mature in the ovary.
Luteinising hormone from the pituitary gland; it stimulates the release of an egg (ovulation).
terms.examiner: Higher tier for the interactions between the hormones.

terms.definition: A hormone that maintains the uterus lining.
terms.examiner: Higher tier: it inhibits FSH and LH.

terms.definition: Oral pills, implants, injections or patches containing hormones that stop eggs maturing or being released.
terms.examiner: Non-hormonal methods include condoms, diaphragms, IUDs, sterilisation and abstinence.

terms.definition: In vitro fertilisation: eggs are collected after FSH and LH treatment, fertilised by sperm in a lab, and one or two embryos are inserted into the uterus.
terms.examiner: Higher tier. Low success rate, multiple births and stress are drawbacks.
